text:
anya: finance ping — monthly cloud bill spiked ~42% overnight, looks concentrated on compute. billing alert shows project=redwood-serving region=us-west1
carl: yep saw that. cost dashboard shows a huge increase in nodegroups/serve-pool on-demand fees
anya: can someone check autoscaler events? suspect runaway launches
devops-bot: Autoscaler event: 1860012350 scaleup from 20 to 120 nodes triggered by queue-length metric
lee: checking infra — serve-pool launch-template v12 has instanceType: a2-highgpu-1, but the deployed node pool template references a2-highcpu-8 (no GPU) ???
maria: wait that's upside down — our committed reservations are for a2-highgpu-1, but templates launched a2-highcpu-8 on-demand
carl: that would explain both cost and performance regressions — paying on-demand for large CPU instances instead of using reserved GPU capacity
anya: pasting the autoscaler config we deployed:
```
kind: NodePool
name: serve-pool
autoscaling:
  min: 10
  max: 120
template:
  instanceType: a2-highcpu-8
  labels:
    role: inference
```
lee: infra repo shows intended instanceType a2-highgpu-1 but TF var got overwritten by CI env var: INSTANCE_FAMILY=highcpu in the deploy pipeline
maria: so terraform applied the wrong template. any runaway nodes still active?
devops-bot: Current nodes: 108 (serve-pool: 108), GPU-tagged nodes: 12
tony: I'll start draining/killing excess nodes, but autoscaler will likely recreate if config not fixed. plan to pause autoscaler first and then scale down
anya: +1 do that. Also open support ticket with cloud to request retroactive committed usage alignment/credit
carl: running command to list infra nodes now: `gcloud compute instances list --filter="labels:role=inference AND status=RUNNING" --format=json | jq '.[] | {name, machineType}'` and saving output
maria: billing SKUs show on-demand CPU-heavy machines — cost per hour ~6x of our reserved GPU unit. I'll draft a billing dispute and flag finance
lee: PR incoming to fix the env var and revert template to a2-highgpu-1; adding a CI gating check to compare intended vs deployed instanceType
anya: kill/scaledown plan: 1) pause autoscaler 2) set max to 30 and scale to 12 GPUs 3) run compliance job to validate instance types 4) unpause autoscaler with safer ramp settings
tony: doing step 1 now
devops-bot: autoscaler paused by tony at 1860012375
carl: uploading node list + billing spike CSV to #finance for visibility
anya: good. once stable we should post a short postmortem. tag:incident-cost-surge :warning:
maria: action items recorded:
- roll back template var in infra repo
- request committed usage credit from cloud provider
- add CI check to block mismatched instanceType deploys
- create alert on unit-cost/token for serve-pool
lee: assigning actions to infra-ops and CI team
anya: thanks everyone, will follow up in the incident doc later.
